skills.name: imagegen
skills.description: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas.

interface.shortDescription: Generate or edit images for websites, games, and more
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $imagegen to make or edit an image for this project.

skills.name: openai-docs
skills.description: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex.
skills.shortDescription: Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, and self-knowledge; OpenAI APIs and ChatGPT Work. 'You'/'this app' means Codex only.

interface.shortDescription: OpenAI and Codex docs for models, skills, tasks, and setup
interface.defaultPrompt: Use OpenAI Docs for official docs lookup, questions about Codex itself or Codex surfaces, model selection, model migration, and prompt-upgrade work.

skills.name: review-agent
skills.description: Perform a read-only, defect-first review of a specified code change and return every actionable finding. Use when another agent delegates review of uncommitted changes, a base-branch diff, a commit, or custom review instructions.

interface.shortDescription: Find actionable bugs in code changes
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $review-agent to review the requested code changes and return actionable findings.

skills.description: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources.

<collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

<multi_agent_mode>Any earlier instruction enabling proactive multi-agent delegation no longer applies. Do not spawn sub-agents unless the user or applicable AGENTS.md/skill instructions explicitly ask for sub-agents, delegation, or parallel agent work.</multi_agent_mode>

{"id": "problem.md", "total_lines": 167, "start": 1, "end": 167, "start_column": 0, "end_column": 29, "requested_end": 180, "has_more": false, "next_start": null, "next_column": 0, "next_end": null, "text": "1: # Conservation of energy for a sphere-valued wave map
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Lawrence C. Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, second edition,
6: Graduate Studies in Mathematics 19, AMS, 2010, section 12.6, exercise 14,
7: printed page 694. The preceding exercise 13 defines the sphere-valued
8: wave map. ISBN: 978-0-8218-4974-3.
9: 
10: > 14. Prove that if \(\mathbf u\) is a wave map into the unit sphere,
11: > with compact support in space, we have conservation of energy:
12: > \[
13: > \frac{d}{dt}\int_{\mathbb R^n}
14: >       |\mathbf u_t|^2+|D\mathbf u|^2\,dx=0.
15: > \]
16: 
17: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
18: 
19: A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
20: the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
21: of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
22: This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
23: correction.
24: 
25: Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
26: \(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
27: Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:
28: 
29: 1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
30: 2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
31:    \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
32:    \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
33:    assumed.
34: 3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
35:    \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
36:    \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).
37: 
38: With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define
39: 
40: \[
41: e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
42: \qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
43: \]
44: 
45: The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
46: \(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
47: Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
48: and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
49: 
50: ## Fixed natural-language proof
51: 
52: ### 1. Tangency and the wave-map equation
53: 
54: Differentiate \(u\cdot u=1\) in time. The product rule gives
55: \(2u\cdot u_t=0\), so
56: 
57: \[
58: u\cdot u_t=0,\qquad
59: u_t\cdot(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu)=a(u_t\cdot u)=0.          \tag{1}
60: \]
61: 
62: No derivative of \(a\) is needed. The familiar explicit equation also
63: follows from the assumptions: twice differentiating the unit constraint
64: gives \(u\cdot u_{tt}=-|u_t|^2\) and
65: \(u\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u=-|\partial_{x_j}u|^2\).
66: Dotting the normality equation with \(u\), using \(|u|^2=1\), yields
67: \(a=\sum_j|\partial_{x_j}u|^2-|u_t|^2\). This is a consequence,
68: not an additional PDE assumption.
69: 
70: ### 2. Common compact support and integrability
71: 
72: Fix \(t_0>0\), put \(J=[t_0/2,3t_0/2]\), and choose its compact
73: spatial set \(C\) from assumption 3. Since \(C\) is bounded, choose
74: \(R>0\) with \(C\subset(-R,R)^n\) and set \(Q=[-R,R]^n\).
75: The box has finite Lebesgue measure \((2R)^n\).
76: 
77: On the open set \((\mathbb R^n\setminus C)\times\operatorname{int}J\),
78: the map equals the constant \(q\), so all its positive-order
79: derivatives vanish. At interior times, \(e\), \(e_t\), and the
80: derivative products used below consequently vanish outside \(C\).
81: They are continuous by smoothness; their spatial sections are measurable,
82: bounded on \(Q\), and supported there. Their absolute integrals are
83: bounded by a finite constant times \(|Q|\). This proves integrability
84: of \(e(\cdot,t_0)\) and of all later terms. Since \(t_0\) was arbitrary,
85: the energy is a finite, well-defined integral at every positive time.
86: 
87: ### 3. Differentiate the energy integral
88: 
89: The product rule and equality of mixed derivatives give
90: 
91: \[
92: e_t=2u_t\cdot u_{tt}
93:    +2\sum_{j=1}^n\partial_{x_j}u\cdot\partial_{x_j}u_t.           \tag{2}
94: \]
95: 
96: Choose \(\eta>0\) so that
97: \([t_0-\eta,t_0+\eta]\subset\operatorname{int}J\).
98: Continuity of (2) on the compact box
99: \(Q\times[t_0-\eta,t_0+\eta]\) gives a finite bound \(|e_t|\leq B\).
100: For \(0<|h|<\eta\), the one-variable mean value theorem at fixed
101: \(x\) therefore gives
102: 
103: \[
104: \left|\frac{e(x,t_0+h)-e(x,t_0)}h\right|
105: \leq B\mathbf1_Q(x).
106: \]
107: 
108: Outside \(Q\), both densities vanish, so the bound holds throughout
109: \(\mathbb R^n\). The right side is integrable. The difference
110: quotients converge pointwise to \(e_t(x,t_0)\). Dominated convergence
111: and linearity for these integrable functions now prove
112: 
113: \[
114: E'(t_0)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e_t(x,t_0)\,dx.            \tag{3}
115: \]
116: 
117: This establishes differentiability of the actual finite integral.
118: 
119: ### 4. Integration by parts and cancellation
120: 
121: For each spatial index \(j\), at time \(t_0\) put
122: \(g_j(x)=u_t(x,t_0)\cdot\partial_{x_j}u(x,t_0)\).

124: because \(C\subset\operatorname{int}Q\). The product rule gives

128: =\partial_{x_j}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_j}u

139: \[

{"id": "problem.md", "total_lines": 167, "start": 1, "end": 167, "start_column": 0, "end_column": 29, "requested_end": 180, "has_more": false, "next_start": null, "next_column": 0, "next_end": null, "text": "1: # Conservation of energy for a sphere-valued wave map
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Lawrence C. Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, second edition,
6: Graduate Studies in Mathematics 19, AMS, 2010, section 12.6, exercise 14,
7: printed page 694. The preceding exercise 13 defines the sphere-valued
8: wave map. ISBN: 978-0-8218-4974-3.
9: 
10: > 14. Prove that if \(\mathbf u\) is a wave map into the unit sphere,
11: > with compact support in space, we have conservation of energy:
12: > \[
13: > \frac{d}{dt}\int_{\mathbb R^n}
14: >       |\mathbf u_t|^2+|D\mathbf u|^2\,dx=0.
15: > \]
16: 
17: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
18: 
19: A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
20: the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
21: of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
22: This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
23: correction.
24: 
25: Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
26: \(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
27: Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:
28: 
29: 1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
30: 2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
31:    \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
32:    \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
33:    assumed.
34: 3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
35:    \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
36:    \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).
37: 
38: With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define
39: 
40: \[
41: e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
42: \qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
43: \]
44: 
45: The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
46: \(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
47: Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
48: and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
49: 
50: ## Fixed natural-language proof
51: 
52: ### 1. Tangency and the wave-map equation
53: 
54: Differentiate \(u\cdot u=1\) in time. The product rule gives
55: \(2u\cdot u_t=0\), so
56: 
57: \[
58: u\cdot u_t=0,\qquad
59: u_t\cdot(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu)=a(u_t\cdot u)=0.          \tag{1}
60: \]
61: 
62: No derivative of \(a\) is needed. The familiar explicit equation also
63: follows from the assumptions: twice differentiating the unit constraint
64: gives \(u\cdot u_{tt}=-|u_t|^2\) and
65: \(u\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u=-|\partial_{x_j}u|^2\).
66: Dotting the normality equation with \(u\), using \(|u|^2=1\), yields
67: \(a=\sum_j|\partial_{x_j}u|^2-|u_t|^2\). This is a consequence,
68: not an additional PDE assumption.
69: 
70: ### 2. Common compact support and integrability
71: 
72: Fix \(t_0>0\), put \(J=[t_0/2,3t_0/2]\), and choose its compact
73: spatial set \(C\) from assumption 3. Since \(C\) is bounded, choose
74: \(R>0\) with \(C\subset(-R,R)^n\) and set \(Q=[-R,R]^n\).
75: The box has finite Lebesgue measure \((2R)^n\).
76: 
77: On the open set \((\mathbb R^n\setminus C)\times\operatorname{int}J\),
78: the map equals the constant \(q\), so all its positive-order
79: derivatives vanish. At interior times, \(e\), \(e_t\), and the
80: derivative products used below consequently vanish outside \(C\).
81: They are continuous by smoothness; their spatial sections are measurable,
82: bounded on \(Q\), and supported there. Their absolute integrals are
83: bounded by a finite constant times \(|Q|\). This proves integrability
84: of \(e(\cdot,t_0)\) and of all later terms. Since \(t_0\) was arbitrary,
85: the energy is a finite, well-defined integral at every positive time.
86: 
87: ### 3. Differentiate the energy integral
88: 
89: The product rule and equality of mixed derivatives give
90: 
91: \[
92: e_t=2u_t\cdot u_{tt}
93:    +2\sum_{j=1}^n\partial_{x_j}u\cdot\partial_{x_j}u_t.           \tag{2}
94: \]
95: 
96: Choose \(\eta>0\) so that
97: \([t_0-\eta,t_0+\eta]\subset\operatorname{int}J\).
98: Continuity of (2) on the compact box
99: \(Q\times[t_0-\eta,t_0+\eta]\) gives a finite bound \(|e_t|\leq B\).
100: For \(0<|h|<\eta\), the one-variable mean value theorem at fixed
101: \(x\) therefore gives
102: 
103: \[
104: \left|\frac{e(x,t_0+h)-e(x,t_0)}h\right|
105: \leq B\mathbf1_Q(x).
106: \]
107: 
108: Outside \(Q\), both densities vanish, so the bound holds throughout
109: \(\mathbb R^n\). The right side is integrable. The difference
110: quotients converge pointwise to \(e_t(x,t_0)\). Dominated convergence
111: and linearity for these integrable functions now prove
112: 
113: \[
114: E'(t_0)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e_t(x,t_0)\,dx.            \tag{3}
115: \]
116: 
117: This establishes differentiability of the actual finite integral.
118: 
119: ### 4. Integration by parts and cancellation
120: 
121: For each spatial index \(j\), at time \(t_0\) put
122: \(g_j(x)=u_t(x,t_0)\cdot\partial_{x_j}u(x,t_0)\).
123: It is smooth and vanishes on a neighborhood of the boundary of \(Q\),
124: because \(C\subset\operatorname{int}Q\). The product rule gives
125: 
126: \[
127: \partial_{x_j}g_j
128: =\partial_{x_j}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_j}u
129:  +u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u.
130: \]
131: 
132: Integrate first over \(x_j\in[-R,R]\) at fixed remaining coordinates.
133: The fundamental theorem of calculus gives zero because both endpoint
134: values of \(g_j\) are zero. Fubini applies on \(Q\) because the
135: derivative and its two summands are continuous and bounded on a
136: finite-measure box. Thus \(\int_Q\partial_{x_j}g_j=0\).
137: All these terms vanish outside \(Q\), so
138: 
139: \[
140: \int_{\mathbb R^n}\partial_{x_j}u\cdot\partial_{x_j}u_t\,dx
141: =-\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u\,dx.              \tag{4}
142: \]
143: 
144: Every integral is finite by step 2. Sum (4) over the finitely many
145: spatial indices and substitute (2) into (3):
146: 
147: \[
148: \begin{aligned}
149: E'(t_0)
150: &=2\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot u_{tt}\,dx
151:  -2\sum_{j=1}^n\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u\,dx\\
152: &=2\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu)\,dx=0,
153: \end{aligned}
154: \]
155: 
156: by (1). This holds at every \(t_0>0\). Hence \(E\) is differentiable
157: with zero derivative on \((0,\infty)\), and is constant there by the
158: mean value theorem. This is conservation of energy with exactly the
159: normalization in the exercise.

{"artifact":{"header":"import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators Topology ContDiff
open MeasureTheory

namespace WM
abbrev X (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ℝ
abbrev Y (m : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)
def dom (n : ℕ) : Set (X n × ℝ) := {p | 0 < p.2}
noncomputable def dt {n : ℕ} {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℝ V] (f : X n × ℝ → V) (x : X n) (t : ℝ) : V := deriv (fun r => f (x,r)) t
noncomputable def dx {n : ℕ} {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℝ V] (f : X n × ℝ → V) (j : Fin n) (x : X n) (t : ℝ) : V := fderiv ℝ (fun y => f (y,t)) x (Pi.single j 1)
noncomputable def ut {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) : X n × ℝ → Y m := fun p => dt u p.1 p.2
noncomputable def utt {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) : X n × ℝ → Y m := fun p => dt (ut u) p.1 p.2
noncomputable def xu {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (j : Fin n) : X n × ℝ → Y m := fun p => dx u j p.1 p.2
noncomputable def lap {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (x : X n) (t : ℝ) : Y m := ∑ j, dx (xu u j) j x t
noncomputable def e {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) : X n × ℝ → ℝ := fun p => ‖ut u p‖ ^ 2 + ∑ j, ‖xu u j p‖ ^ 2
noncomputable def et {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) : X n × ℝ → ℝ := fun p => dt (e u) p.1 p.2
noncomputable def energy {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (t : ℝ) : ℝ := ∫ x, e u (x,t)
def box (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (X n) := {x | ∀ j, x j ∈ Set.Icc (-R) R}
def openBox (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (X n) := {x | ∀ j, x j ∈ Set.Ioo (-R) R}
noncomputable def aTerm {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) : X n × ℝ → ℝ := fun p => inner ℝ (ut u p) (utt u p)
noncomputable def bTerm {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (j : Fin n) : X n × ℝ → ℝ := fun p => inner ℝ (xu u j p) (dx (ut u) j p.1 p.2)
noncomputable def cTerm {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (j : Fin n) : X n × ℝ → ℝ := fun p => inner ℝ (ut u p) (dx (xu u j) j p.1 p.2)
noncomputable def flux {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (j : Fin n) : X n × ℝ → ℝ := fun p => inner ℝ (ut u p) (xu u j p)
noncomputable def divFlux {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (j : Fin n) : X n × ℝ → ℝ := fun p => dx (flux u j) j p.1 p.2
def regular {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) : Prop :=
  ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (ut u) (dom n) ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (utt u) (dom n) ∧ (∀ j, ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (xu u j) (dom n)) ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (e u) (dom n) ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (et u) (dom n) ∧
  (∀ x t, 0 < t → et u (x,t) = 2 * aTerm u (x,t) + 2 * ∑ j, bTerm u j (x,t)) ∧
  (∀ j x t, 0 < t → dt (xu u j) x t = dx (ut u) j x t)
def good {n : ℕ} (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) (f : X n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  Continuous f ∧ (∃ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B ∧ ∀ x ∈ box n R, |f x| ≤ B) ∧ (∀ x, x ∉ C → f x = 0) ∧ Integrable f
noncomputable def quot {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (t h : ℝ) (x : X n) : ℝ := (e u (x,t+h) - e u (x,t)) / h
noncomputable def major {n : ℕ} (R B : ℝ) : X n → ℝ := (box n R).indicator (fun _ => B)
def geometry {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (q : Y m) (τ : ℝ) (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  IsCompact C ∧ 0 < R ∧ C ⊆ openBox n R ∧ (∀ x, x ∉ C → ∀ r ∈ Set.Icc (τ/2) (3*τ/2), u (x,r) = q)
def localData {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (q : Y m) (τ : ℝ) (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  geometry u q τ C R ∧ IsCompact (box n R) ∧ volume (box n R) = ENNReal.ofReal ((2*R)^n) ∧ volume (box n R) < ⊤ ∧
  (∀ x, x ∉ C → ∀ r ∈ Set.Ioo (τ/2) (3*τ/2), ∀ k : ℕ, 0 < k → iteratedFDeriv ℝ k u (x,r) = 0) ∧
  (∀ r ∈ Set.Ioo (τ/2) (3*τ/2), good C R (fun x => e u (x,r)) ∧ good C R (fun x => et u (x,r)) ∧ good C R (fun x => aTerm u (x,r)) ∧ ∀ j, good C R (fun x => bTerm u j (x,r)) ∧ good C R (fun x => cTerm u j (x,r)) ∧ good C R (fun x => divFlux u j (x,r)))
def supportAndRegularity {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (q : Y m) : Prop :=
  regular u ∧ (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → Integrable (fun x => e u (x,t))) ∧ ∀ τ : ℝ, 0 < τ → ∃ C R, localData u q τ C R
noncomputable def fluxData {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (q : Y m) (t : ℝ) (j : Fin n) (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  localData u q t C R ∧ ContDiff ℝ ∞ (fun x => flux u j (x,t)) ∧ good C R (fun x => flux u j (x,t)) ∧
  (∀ x, divFlux u j (x,t) = bTerm u j (x,t) + cTerm u j (x,t))
end WM

X n is the real coordinate space Fin n → ℝ, with its standard finite product Lebesgue volume. Its library sup norm is only an auxiliary coordinate topology: it has the same topology and derivative calculus as Euclidean ℝ^n; no spatial-vector norm occurs in the energy. Y m carries the Euclidean inner product and norm. Fin n indexes the original n coordinates with a zero-based relabeling. u is a total extension to all real times; H002 is smoothness only on the open set t>0, and all physical hypotheses and conclusions are restricted to t>0. Any original u extends by q at nonpositive times; conversely restriction recovers the original map. Germ-local derivatives at positive times and energy there are independent of the extension. dx is the spatial Fréchet derivative applied to the standard coordinate vector, dt the ordinary time derivative. On the smooth open domain these are the usual partial derivatives. All norms of derivatives in e are Euclidean target norms, hence its finite sum is precisely the Frobenius square, without a half. lap is the sum of the unmixed second spatial partials. The propositions regular, geometry, good, localData, supportAndRegularity and fluxData are transparent bundles of obligations, not assumptions or proved facts. artifact.header:
import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators Topology ContDiff
open MeasureTheory

namespace WM
abbrev X (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ℝ
abbrev Y (m : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)
def dom (n : ℕ) : Set (X n × ℝ) := {p | 0 < p.2}
noncomputable def dt {n : ℕ} {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℝ V] (f : X n × ℝ → V) (x : X n) (t : ℝ) : V := deriv (fun r => f (x,r)) t
noncomputable def dx {n : ℕ} {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℝ V] (f : X n × ℝ → V) (j : Fin n) (x : X n) (t : ℝ) : V := fderiv ℝ (fun y => f (y,t)) x (Pi.single j 1)
noncomputable def ut {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) : X n × ℝ → Y m := fun p => dt u p.1 p.2
noncomputable def utt {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) : X n × ℝ → Y m := fun p => dt (ut u) p.1 p.2
noncomputable def xu {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (j : Fin n) : X n × ℝ → Y m := fun p => dx u j p.1 p.2
noncomputable def lap {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (x : X n) (t : ℝ) : Y m := ∑ j, dx (xu u j) j x t
noncomputable def e {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) : X n × ℝ → ℝ := fun p => ‖ut u p‖ ^ 2 + ∑ j, ‖xu u j p‖ ^ 2
noncomputable def et {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) : X n × ℝ → ℝ := fun p => dt (e u) p.1 p.2
noncomputable def energy {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (t : ℝ) : ℝ := ∫ x, e u (x,t)
def box (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (X n) := {x | ∀ j, x j ∈ Set.Icc (-R) R}
def openBox (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (X n) := {x | ∀ j, x j ∈ Set.Ioo (-R) R}
noncomputable def aTerm {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) : X n × ℝ → ℝ := fun p => inner ℝ (ut u p) (utt u p)
noncomputable def bTerm {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (j : Fin n) : X n × ℝ → ℝ := fun p => inner ℝ (xu u j p) (dx (ut u) j p.1 p.2)
noncomputable def cTerm {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (j : Fin n) : X n × ℝ → ℝ := fun p => inner ℝ (ut u p) (dx (xu u j) j p.1 p.2)
noncomputable def flux {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (j : Fin n) : X n × ℝ → ℝ := fun p => inner ℝ (ut u p) (xu u j p)
noncomputable def divFlux {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (j : Fin n) : X n × ℝ → ℝ := fun p => dx (flux u j) j p.1 p.2
def regular {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) : Prop :=
  ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (ut u) (dom n) ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (utt u) (dom n) ∧ (∀ j, ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (xu u j) (dom n)) ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (e u) (dom n) ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (et u) (dom n) ∧
  (∀ x t, 0 < t → et u (x,t) = 2 * aTerm u (x,t) + 2 * ∑ j, bTerm u j (x,t)) ∧
  (∀ j x t, 0 < t → dt (xu u j) x t = dx (ut u) j x t)
def good {n : ℕ} (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) (f : X n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  Continuous f ∧ (∃ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B ∧ ∀ x ∈ box n R, |f x| ≤ B) ∧ (∀ x, x ∉ C → f x = 0) ∧ Integrable f
noncomputable def quot {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (t h : ℝ) (x : X n) : ℝ := (e u (x,t+h) - e u (x,t)) / h
noncomputable def major {n : ℕ} (R B : ℝ) : X n → ℝ := (box n R).indicator (fun _ => B)
def geometry {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (q : Y m) (τ : ℝ) (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  IsCompact C ∧ 0 < R ∧ C ⊆ openBox n R ∧ (∀ x, x ∉ C → ∀ r ∈ Set.Icc (τ/2) (3*τ/2), u (x,r) = q)
def localData {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (q : Y m) (τ : ℝ) (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  geometry u q τ C R ∧ IsCompact (box n R) ∧ volume (box n R) = ENNReal.ofReal ((2*R)^n) ∧ volume (box n R) < ⊤ ∧
  (∀ x, x ∉ C → ∀ r ∈ Set.Ioo (τ/2) (3*τ/2), ∀ k : ℕ, 0 < k → iteratedFDeriv ℝ k u (x,r) = 0) ∧
  (∀ r ∈ Set.Ioo (τ/2) (3*τ/2), good C R (fun x => e u (x,r)) ∧ good C R (fun x => et u (x,r)) ∧ good C R (fun x => aTerm u (x,r)) ∧ ∀ j, good C R (fun x => bTerm u j (x,r)) ∧ good C R (fun x => cTerm u j (x,r)) ∧ good C R (fun x => divFlux u j (x,r)))
def supportAndRegularity {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (q : Y m) : Prop :=
  regular u ∧ (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → Integrable (fun x => e u (x,t))) ∧ ∀ τ : ℝ, 0 < τ → ∃ C R, localData u q τ C R
noncomputable def fluxData {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → Y m) (q : Y m) (t : ℝ) (j : Fin n) (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  localData u q t C R ∧ ContDiff ℝ ∞ (fun x => flux u j (x,t)) ∧ good C R (fun x => flux u j (x,t)) ∧
  (∀ x, divFlux u j (x,t) = bTerm u j (x,t) + cTerm u j (x,t))
end WM

premise_types.H005: ∀ (x : WM.X n) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → ∃ a : ℝ, WM.utt u (x,t) - WM.lap u x t = a • u (x,t)
premise_types.H006: ∀ (s t : ℝ), 0 < s → s < t → ∃ C : Set (WM.X n), IsCompact C ∧ ∀ x, x ∉ C → ∀ r ∈ Set.Icc s t, u (x,r) = q

artifact.conclusion_type: (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → Integrable (fun x => WM.e u (x,t))) ∧ DifferentiableOn ℝ (WM.energy u) (Set.Ioi 0) ∧ (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → deriv (WM.energy u) t = 0) ∧ (∀ s t : ℝ, 0 < s → 0 < t → WM.energy u s = WM.energy u t)
artifact.representation: PENDING_AUDIT_B. X n is the real coordinate space Fin n → ℝ, with its standard finite product Lebesgue volume. Its library sup norm is only an auxiliary coordinate topology: it has the same topology and derivative calculus as Euclidean ℝ^n; no spatial-vector norm occurs in the energy. Y m carries the Euclidean inner product and norm. Fin n indexes the original n coordinates with a zero-based relabeling. u is a total extension to all real times; H002 is smoothness only on the open set t>0, and all physical hypotheses and conclusions are restricted to t>0. Any original u extends by q at nonpositive times; conversely restriction recovers the original map. Germ-local derivatives at positive times and energy there are independent of the extension. dx is the spatial Fréchet derivative applied to the standard coordinate vector, dt the ordinary time derivative. On the smooth open domain these are the usual partial derivatives. All norms of derivatives in e are Euclidean target norms, hence its finite sum is precisely the Frobenius square, without a half. lap is the sum of the unmixed second spatial partials. The propositions regular, geometry, good, localData, supportAndRegularity and fluxData are transparent bundles of obligations, not assumptions or proved facts. Bochner Integrable for real sections means absolute Lebesgue integrability; the total integral definition is only used as finite energy after T004. For the one actual coordinate split in Fubini, T010 explicitly checks the insertion map's measure preservation, box image, and integral conversion; this stays in finite product coordinates, including the zero-dimensional remainder.

steps.statement: WM.regular u

For the one actual coordinate split in Fubini, T010 explicitly checks the insertion map's measure preservation, box image, and integral conversion; this stays in finite product coordinates, including the zero-dimensional remainder.
